`{{x}}` is escaped for where it lands (api({at:'frontend'}) ssr_mustache_escaping); `{{{x}}}` writes sanitized HTML; `{{{{x}}}}` writes the value unescaped (only for trusted HTML). Dot paths read nested values and rows: `{{user.email}}`, `{{rows.0.title}}`.

Sections: `{{#rows}}…{{/rows}}` repeats per row (or shows once for a truthy value); `{{^rows}}…{{/rows}}` shows when empty. `{{#if status = "active"}}…{{else}}…{{/if}}` compares with = != > < >= <= (numbers when both sides are numbers); `{{#role "editor,reviewer"}}…{{/role}}` shows to a viewer who holds any listed role by name (the account's role, the role on their membership row in the current tenant, a role grant) and to the app's global admin, who sees every role section. `{{#role "admin"}}` (any letter case, also inside a list) shows to a global admin only (`_benmore_users.role` = admin or an admin grant with no group): a tenant member whose membership role is `admin` does not open it, and opens other role sections only by the roles they hold. For content a tenant's own admins see, write `{{#if user.app_role = "admin"}}…{{/if}}` (user.app_role is the viewer's role in their current tenant); `benmore check` warns about an `admin` role section in an app whose tenant members can hold that role. A section hides markup, it is not access control: the page's queries and the API rules decide what the viewer can read; `{{#switch status}}{{#case "a"}}…{{#default}}…{{/switch}}`.

Directives (mustache only, compiled to HTMX): `<form :create="tasks">` posts to /api/tasks; `:patch="/api/tasks/{{id}}" :set="done=1"`; `:delete="tasks" :id="{{id}}"` (asks "Are you sure?"); `:validate="required,email,minlen:8"` on inputs. `:confirm="Sure?"` sets the confirmation text and works only when written after `:delete`, or after a `:patch="/url"` that has no `:set`, on the same element. Anywhere else (with `:patch … :set`, before `:delete`, on a plain hx-* element) it is left in the markup and does nothing: write `hx-confirm="Sure?"` there.

The write gate refuses another engine's syntax in a mustache page, naming it and what to write instead: Handlebars `{{>partial}}`, `{{#each}}`, `{{#unless}}`, `{{else if}}` and `{{#with}}`; Vue `v-*` and `@event`; React `className=`, `htmlFor=` and camelCase handlers; Angular directives; a nested `<page>`; a Tailwind CDN `<link>`; and auth paths the framework does not serve (`/auth/...`, `/api/auth/...`).
